title: The Part of the Cancellation Fee a Given-Up Plan Is Charged At
content:
How much of the cancellation fee a Pass and Trip Protection plan is charged at when it is given up is settled
from the day the plan was taken and from how much of its term has run.

1. Where the plan is given up no later than its free look period, counted in calendar days from the day the
   plan was taken with the anchor day counting as day zero, the part of the fee the charge stands at is
   nothing.
2. Where more than half of the term has run, the part of the fee the charge stands at is half of it.
3. In every other case the part of the fee the charge stands at is the whole of it.

**The free look period each plan carries.**

| Plan | Free look period (calendar days) |
| --- | --- |
| Season Pass Protection Basic | 10 |
| Season Pass Protection Plus | 14 |
| Season Pass Protection Premier | 14 |
| Collective Trip Protection Standard | 14 |
| Collective Trip Protection Elite | 21 |
| Collective Total Protection Concierge | 30 |

**Reading the ladder.** The three are read in the order given, so a plan given up inside its free look period
stands at nothing however much of the term has run. Past the free look period the question is only whether
more than half of the term has run: exactly half is not more than half, and the plan stands at the whole of
the fee.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical inputs).** A plan whose free look period is 14 calendar days, given up on the
fourteenth day after it was taken, stands at nothing; given up on the fifteenth day with a fifth of the term
run, it stands at the whole of the fee; given up with three fifths of the term run, it stands at half of the
fee.
